title: Subsets II
description:
# Subsets II

Given an integer array `nums` that may contain duplicate values, return all unique subsets of `nums`.

A subset may use each input position at most once. Because duplicate values can create the same subset through different positions, the answer must contain each value multiset only once. The judge accepts the subsets in any outer order; the examples show each subset in nondecreasing order for readability.

Include the empty subset `[]`, which selects no elements.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [1,2,2]
**Output:** [[],[1],[1,2],[1,2,2],[2],[2,2]]

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [0]
**Output:** [[],[0]]

## Constraints:

* `1 <= nums.length <= 10`
* `-10 <= nums[i] <= 10`

solutions.name: Sort and Skip Same-Depth Duplicates
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort `nums`, record the current path as one subset, and try each later index as the next chosen value. If a value equals the previous value at the same recursion depth, skip it because the previous branch already generated every subset starting with that value at this depth.

## Key Insight

Duplicates are only illegal when they start a second identical branch at the same depth. A later depth may still choose the same value, which is how subsets like `[2,2]` remain valid.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^n)
- Space Complexity: O(n) excluding the returned subsets

solutions.name: Run-Length Count Recursion
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort the array and process one run of equal values at a time. For a run with value `v` and count `c`, recursively choose 0 copies, then 1 copy, up to `c` copies before moving to the next distinct value.

## Key Insight

The answer is defined by how many copies of each distinct value are used. Modeling a duplicate run as a count choice removes duplicate branches entirely instead of detecting and skipping them after the fact.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * U), where U is the number of unique subsets
- Space Complexity: O(n) excluding the returned subsets

solutions.name: Iterative Previous-Layer Expansion
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort the values and build subsets iteratively. For a new value, extend every subset that already exists. For a duplicate value, extend only the subsets created during the previous occurrence of that same value.

## Key Insight

When processing the second or later copy of a value, attaching it to older subsets would recreate subsets that were already produced by the first copy. The previous layer marks the only subsets that can legally receive the next duplicate.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * U), where U is the number of unique subsets
- Space Complexity: O(n * U) for the returned subsets

solutions.name: Canonical Bit Mask Enumeration
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort the array and enumerate every bit mask. A mask is canonical only if it never chooses a later duplicate while leaving the previous equal value unchosen; valid masks are converted into subsets and added to the answer.

## Key Insight

For each run of equal values, the chosen bits must form a prefix of that run. This keeps exactly one mask for each possible copy count while preserving the direct bit-mask interpretation of a subset.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^n)
- Space Complexity: O(n * U) for the returned subsets

tests.description: Canonical duplicate input where two positions with value 2 must not create duplicate rows.
Single element input still has exactly two subsets.
All elements equal produce one subset for each possible copy count.
Unsorted input requires sorting before duplicate control.
Duplicate values separated by another value still collapse after sorting.
Negative duplicate values and zero are both preserved correctly.
Constraint boundary values verify duplicate handling at the numeric extremes.
Two duplicate groups require independent count choices.
A triple duplicate run with a distinct smaller value checks run-length logic.
Mixed negative, zero, and positive values with duplicates verify ordering-independent correctness.
Four equal values catch solutions that only remove adjacent duplicate branches once.
Unsorted mixed-sign input with one duplicate group covers another realistic ordering.
